itineraries.title: Pride, Art & a Jam Band in Raleigh
itineraries.theme: Free downtown festival energy capped by a big amphitheater show
itineraries.overview: A car-light downtown Raleigh day: free, family-friendly art at the NC Museum of Art in the morning, the Out! Raleigh Pride street festival all afternoon on Fayetteville Street, then jam-band Goose at Red Hat Amphitheater to close the night. It's a hot one — hydrate and plan an AC break midday.

morning.title: America250: Knowing the West Community Day
morning.location: NC Museum of Art, 2110 Blue Ridge Rd
morning.notes: Hands-on artmaking, live music, and guided tours — air-conditioned galleries before the heat peaks.

afternoon.title: Out! Raleigh Pride Festival
afternoon.notes: ~100 vendors, two stages, kids zone, and a beer garden. Shade is limited — bring a hat and water.

evening.title: An Evening with Goose
evening.location: Red Hat Amphitheater, 500 S McDowell St
evening.notes: Outdoor amphitheater two blocks from the festival footprint — easy to roll right over.

food.notes: Fully vegetarian/vegan; a short walk off Fayetteville St. Reserve ahead on festival days.
Grab an early table before the show, or graze the festival's beer garden food vendors.

alternatives.good_weather: Stroll the full Fayetteville St footprint and the kids zone
alternatives.rain: Duck into the air-conditioned NC Museum of History or Marbles a block away until the pop-up storm passes
Red Hat is open-air — pack a poncho; storms this week are brief afternoon cells that usually clear by showtime

practical_notes: Park once downtown (decks on Wilmington/Blount) and walk the whole day.
Heat advisory territory (mid-90s°F) — refill water and take a midday AC break.
Red Hat doors are typically ~60–90 min before show; bag policy is clear-bag only.

itineraries.title: Durham Makers, Museums & Dex Fest
itineraries.theme: Handmade goods, contemporary art, and homegrown indie rock
itineraries.drive_time: Durham core + 15 min to Carrboro for the show
itineraries.overview: A creative Durham Saturday: browse 50+ local crafters at Durham Central Park, take in Dyani White Hawk's acclaimed video installation at the Nasher (free), then head to Carrboro for night two of Dex Fest at the legendary Cat's Cradle.

morning.title: Durham Craft Market
morning.notes: Beat the heat — go early. Pair it with the adjacent Durham Farmers' Market stalls.

afternoon.title: Dyani White Hawk: LISTEN
afternoon.location: Nasher Museum of Art at Duke, 2001 Campus Dr
afternoon.notes: Eight-channel video installation; free admission. Cool, quiet, and air-conditioned.

evening.title: Dex Fest Night Two
evening.location: Cat's Cradle, 300 E Main St, Carrboro
evening.notes: Doors 6pm. Carrboro is ~15 min west; park on Main St or the East End deck.

food.vegan_dish: Vegan Margherita with house vegan mozzarella
food.notes: Walkable from Durham Central Park; fast and vegan-friendly.
On the way to Carrboro; deep vegan menu. Or grab a vegan deli plate at Weaver Street Market next to the Cradle.

alternatives.good_weather: Linger at the open-air pavilion and food trucks
alternatives.rain: The pavilion is covered; vendors stay open through light rain

alternatives.good_weather: Walk Carrboro's Main St before the show
alternatives.rain: Cat's Cradle is indoors — no weather worries once you're in

practical_notes: Nasher is free but timed-entry on busy days — reserve a slot online.
Dex Fest is a two-room festival; check set times so you don't miss headliners.
Carrboro parking fills on show nights — arrive by 6:15.

itineraries.title: Cary: Market Morning to Symphony Night
itineraries.theme: Easygoing suburban Saturday, classical music under the stars
itineraries.overview: A relaxed Cary day built for families: a producer-only farmers' market in Morrisville, an afternoon at Downtown Cary Park, then the NC Symphony performing the music of Billy Joel under the stars at Koka Booth Amphitheatre.

morning.title: Western Wake Farmers' Market
morning.notes: Local produce, baked goods, and prepared foods. Vegan and vegetarian stalls available.

afternoon.title: Downtown Cary Park (self-guided)
afternoon.notes: Splash fountains, shaded lawns, and the play areas — an easy midday break before the amphitheater.

evening.title: The Music of Billy Joel with Tony DeSare (NC Symphony)
evening.notes: Bring a blanket and a picnic; lawn seating. Gates open ~90 min early.

food.vegan_dish: Masala dosa with sambar & coconut chutney
food.notes: Fully vegetarian; many vegan options — ask for no ghee.
Koka Booth allows picnics/coolers for symphony shows — pack ahead, or buy from on-site vendors.

alternatives.rain: Shop and café-hop along Academy/Chatham St under cover
Koka Booth covered pavilion seats stay dry; lawn folks should bring ponchos

practical_notes: Confirm Koka Booth's picnic/cooler policy for this show before packing glass.
Mosquitoes near the lake at dusk — bring repellent.
Free parking at Koka Booth fills early on symphony nights.

itineraries.title: Sunday Markets & Free Music, Durham to Chapel Hill
itineraries.theme: Lazy free-music Sunday across three towns
itineraries.drive_time: Durham → Carrboro → Chapel Hill, ~20 min total hops
itineraries.overview: An almost-free Sunday strung together by live music: a vendor market at Durham Central Park, brunch music on the lawn at Weaver Street Market in Carrboro, an interactive public-art installation at the Ackland, and a sunset concert at Southern Village.

morning.title: Durham Underground Market
morning.notes: 50+ vendors, live musicians, and food trucks under the pavilion.

afternoon.title: Sunday Brunch Music: Saludos Compay
afternoon.notes: Grab a deli plate and a spot on the lawn — quintessential Carrboro.

afternoon.title: pARC by The Urban Conga
afternoon.notes: Interactive outdoor art; pop inside the free Ackland galleries to cool off.

evening.title: Sundays at Sundown: Capital Transit
evening.notes: Lawn concert; bring chairs and tip the band. Dinner on the village plaza first.

food.notes: Self-serve hot bar and deli right where the brunch music plays.

food.place: Town Hall Grill / Southern Village plaza
food.notes: Several plaza spots steps from the concert green.

alternatives.good_weather: Play on the outdoor pARC installation
alternatives.rain: Move into the free, air-conditioned Ackland galleries
If storms roll in, the village's covered patios and shops keep you close until it clears

practical_notes: This whole day can be done for the price of food + gas.
Carrboro and Southern Village both have easy free parking on Sundays.
Afternoon storm chance is slight but real — keep a small umbrella in the car.

itineraries.title: Butterflies by Day, Bulls by Night
itineraries.theme: Family science museum + Triple-A fireworks night
itineraries.overview: A classic Durham family day: the Museum of Life and Science (Butterfly House, Dinosaur Trail, live animals) when it's hottest, then Triple-A baseball as the Durham Bulls host the Gwinnett Stripers on an Independence-week fireworks night at the historic DBAP.

morning.title: Museum of Life and Science
morning.notes: Indoor + shaded outdoor exhibits; the Butterfly House is a cool, humid escape. (Open daily through the week.)

afternoon.title: AC break / downtown Durham stroll
afternoon.notes: It hits 101°F — retreat to the shaded ATC boardwalk and shops near the ballpark.

evening.title: Durham Bulls vs. Gwinnett Stripers
evening.location: Durham Bulls Athletic Park, 409 Blackwell St
evening.notes: Independence-week homestand with fireworks nights — arrive early for a good lawn/berm spot.

food.notes: Light lunch; save room for the ballpark.

food.vegetarian_dish: Veggie burger at the café next door
food.notes: DBAP has a few veg options; Tobacco Road Café overlooks the field.

alternatives.rain: Plenty of indoor exhibits keep the day going

alternatives.good_weather: Lawn berm seating for the fireworks
alternatives.rain: DBAP delays for storms — keep an eye on the forecast; covered concourse if a cell passes

practical_notes: Hottest day of the window (101°F) — sunscreen, water, and midday shade are essential.
DBAP fireworks nights sell out the berm; buy tickets ahead.
Park in the ATC decks and walk to the gates.

itineraries.title: Historic Raleigh: Trolley, Tours & a Pop Show
itineraries.theme: City history by day, big pop concert by night
itineraries.drive_time: Downtown Raleigh + 12 min to Walnut Creek
itineraries.overview: A history-buff's Raleigh Saturday: a guided tour of Mordecai Historic Park (birthplace of President Andrew Johnson), the hour-long Historic Raleigh trolley, treasure-hunting at the Raleigh Market, then Meghan Trainor's The Get In Girl Tour at Coastal Credit Union Music Park.

morning.title: Mordecai Historic Park Guided Tour
morning.notes: Tours leave the Visitor Center on the hour, 10am–3pm.

morning.title: Historic Raleigh Trolley Tour
morning.notes: One-hour narrated loop of historic downtown; departs 11, 12, 1, 2.

afternoon.title: The Raleigh Market
afternoon.notes: Antiques, crafts, and collectibles; free admission and parking. Indoor + outdoor — some AC relief.

evening.title: Meghan Trainor: The Get In Girl Tour
evening.location: Coastal Credit Union Music Park at Walnut Creek
evening.notes: Outdoor amphitheater ~12 min from downtown; with Icona Pop.

food.notes: Near Mordecai/Person St; lots of veg-friendly cafés in the Oakwood area.

food.vegan_dish: Vegan arepa with black beans, avocado & plantain
food.notes: Fast and on the way to Walnut Creek; build-your-own with vegan options.

alternatives.rain: Head for the indoor buildings; the market runs rain or shine
Walnut Creek lawn is exposed — bring a poncho; pavilion seats stay dry

practical_notes: Buy the Mordecai tour + trolley combo at the Visitor Center; they sell out on nice Saturdays.
Walnut Creek is clear-bag only; gates ~90 min before showtime.
Afternoon storms are brief — they usually clear before the 6:30 gates.
